name: F-6
tagline: Embassy-side sector with the calmest tree-lined streets
description: F-6 sits between Blue Area and the Margalla Hills, closest to the Diplomatic Enclave, and is the most established of Islamabad's sectors. Its sub-blocks hold walled bungalows under mature trees, while F-6 Markaz, known as Super Market, carries bookshops, bakeries, salons and long-running restaurants. Most embassy staff and expats live here.
bestFor: Nomads who want the quietest, greenest central address and easy embassy access.
pros: Closest sector to the Diplomatic Enclave
Quiet, shaded streets with big gardens
Super Market covers most daily errands
cons: Mostly whole houses, few short-term flats
Almost nothing open late at night

name: F-7
tagline: Jinnah Super, the liveliest sector in Islamabad
description: F-7 is the social heart of the city, built around Jinnah Super Market and the smaller Bhittai Road strip, with cafes, third-wave coffee roasters, restaurants and boutiques. Residential blocks behind are quiet and well-kept, and the Margalla trailheads for Trail 3 and 5 start at the top of the sector.
bestFor: Remote workers who want cafes to work from and hiking trails ten minutes away.
pros: Best cafe and restaurant density in the city
Margalla Hills trailheads within a short drive
Central for both Blue Area and the embassies
cons: Markaz parking and traffic get chaotic
Load shedding still cuts power in summer

name: F-11
tagline: Modern apartments and the best value in the F sectors
description: F-11 is a newer western sector where apartment buildings actually outnumber bungalows, which is unusual in Islamabad and makes it the easiest place to rent a furnished flat. F-11 Markaz has fast food chains, gyms, grocery stores and a cinema, and it sits close to the Kashmir Highway for airport runs.
bestFor: Nomads who want a furnished apartment with a lift, a gym and a short lease.
pros: Most furnished apartments available to rent
Well-stocked markaz with gyms and groceries
Quick access to the highway and airport
cons: Newer and blander than the older sectors
Fifteen to twenty minutes from Blue Area
Some buildings have unreliable lifts and water

name: E-11
tagline: Cheaper high-rises right under the Margallas
description: E-11 is the most affordable of the western sectors, built up with private housing societies and multi-storey apartment blocks pressed against the Margalla foothills. Rents run well below the F sectors and the sector has grown its own markets, clinics and eateries, though roads and drainage lag behind the planned sectors.
bestFor: Budget-minded long-stayers who want hill views and lower rent than the F sectors.
pros: Cheapest apartment rents on this side of the city
Margalla Hills views and cooler evening air
Plenty of new-build flats to choose from
cons: Patchy road quality and drainage in monsoon
Longer commute to the city centre
Water supply and power cuts are more frequent

name: G-11
tagline: Quiet middle-class sector with a metro stop
description: G-11 is a settled residential sector south of F-11, planned around a central markaz with vegetable markets, banks and small restaurants. Streets are wide and low-rise, with families rather than expats, and the Metro Bus running along the Kashmir Highway connects it to Blue Area and Rawalpindi cheaply.
bestFor: Longer stays where cost and a real neighbourhood matter more than nightlife.
pros: Metro Bus station for cheap central trips
Rents well below the F sectors
Quiet streets and a practical local market
cons: Very few cafes suited to working in
Dead in the evenings, you go elsewhere to eat
